summary: Creating a GitHub OAuth app is a fully self‑serve process that takes a few minutes: a logged‑in user with a verified email fills a short web form at the GitHub settings page, provides basic metadata (app name, homepage, callback URL) and saves the app; there is no monetary cost or mandatory review, though a flagged account cannot complete the flow.

selfServeMinutes.reasoning: The form consists of a handful of fields (name, description, homepage URL, callback URL, optional privacy/terms URLs) which can be entered in roughly five to ten minutes of keyboard time.

reviewWaitBusinessDays.reasoning: GitHub does not publish a review queue for OAuth apps; apps appear immediately after creation unless the account is flagged.

steps.title: Open New OAuth App page
steps.detail: Navigate to https://github.com/settings/applications/new (or Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App).

steps.title: Enter application details
steps.detail: Provide Application name, Homepage URL, optional Description, and Authorization callback URL.

steps.title: Register application
steps.detail: Click the “Register application” button to create the OAuth app.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret
steps.detail: After registration, copy the generated Client ID and Client Secret for use in your application.

nuances.title: Read vs write scopes
nuances.detail: OAuth apps can request read or write access to your GitHub data; choose scopes carefully to follow the principle of least privilege.

citations.quote: OAuth apps can have *read* or *write* access to your GitHub data.
citations.title: Authorizing OAuth apps

nuances.title: Token capabilities
nuances.detail: A token inherits the permissions of its owner and is further limited by the scopes granted to it.

citations.quote: A token has the same capabilities to access resources and perform actions on those resources that the owner of the token has, and is further limited by any scopes or permissions granted to the token.
citations.title: Authorizing OAuth apps

nuances.title: Token creation limits
nuances.detail: GitHub limits each user/application/scope combination to ten active tokens and caps token creation at ten per hour. Exceeding these limits may cause token creation to fail.

citations.quote: There is a limit of ten tokens that are issued per user/application/scope combination, and a rate limit of ten tokens created per hour.
citations.title: Authorizing OAuth apps

nuances.title: Token revocation on overflow
nuances.detail: If more than ten tokens are created for the same user and scopes, GitHub automatically revokes an existing token in that combination.
